questions.prompt: A memoized Counter updates its own state while props stay equal. What should you expect?

choices.text: A render, because memo does not block its own state updates.
No render, because memo freezes every local state value.
A remount, because memo requires replacing the component type.
A render only if the parent replaces every prop object first.

questions.explanation: memo optimizes parent-driven prop comparisons. It does not prevent the component own state from updating.

sources.title: memo
sources.claim: memo may skip parent-driven renders when props compare equal by Object.is, but own state or used context updates still render; fresh object and function props can defeat memoization.

questions.prompt: A memoized component reads a context value that changes. What does memo guarantee?

choices.text: It permanently freezes the context captured on first render.
It hides every context update until a prop changes.
It does not prevent rendering for changes in used context.
It converts context into a mutable module-level variable.

questions.explanation: memo compares props, not a prohibition on context-driven updates.

sources.title: memo
sources.claim: memo may skip parent-driven renders when props compare equal by Object.is, but own state or used context updates still render; fresh object and function props can defeat memoization.

questions.prompt: A costly filter uses items and query. What dependency list preserves a useful correct cache?

choices.text: [items.length], because equal lengths guarantee equal item contents.
[Math.random()], because every render should reuse the same value.
[], because the first calculation must stay correct forever.
[items, query], including the values used by the calculation.

questions.explanation: Both data and query affect filtering. Omitting dependencies can retain a stale result; unstable dependencies prevent cache reuse.

sources.title: useMemo
sources.claim: useMemo caches a pure calculation between renders while dependencies compare equal by Object.is; it is a performance optimization rather than a semantic guarantee.

questions.prompt: Why should code remain correct if a useMemo cache is discarded?

choices.text: useMemo guarantees every cache persists through every future mount.
It is a performance optimization, not essential application storage.
useMemo preserves its cached value as a correctness guarantee across every remount.
It should replace state whenever a value must survive later renders reliably.

questions.explanation: React may discard caches. State or another durable model should carry correctness requirements.

sources.title: useMemo
sources.claim: useMemo caches a pure calculation between renders while dependencies compare equal by Object.is; it is a performance optimization rather than a semantic guarantee.

questions.prompt: A parent passes options={{sort: "name"}} to a memoized child on every render. Why may the child still render?

choices.text: Object.is recursively sees that nested sort strings are equal.
Every options prop is ignored automatically by memo comparison.
A fresh options object is not equal to the previous object reference.
memo skips all children whenever their rendered text is unchanged.

questions.explanation: Default prop comparison is shallow Object.is. Recreating an object can defeat the boundary.

sources.title: memo
sources.claim: memo compares each prop with Object.is; fresh object or function references prevent a default props-equal result.

questions.prompt: What does Profiler actualDuration help assess?

choices.text: Time spent rendering the profiled subtree for the current update.
Network request duration for every browser navigation automatically.
Total database time used by all server queries behind the page.
Time spent painting every pixel by the browser GPU exclusively.

questions.explanation: Profiler measures React render work. It should not be mistaken for network or browser-paint duration.

sources.title: Profiler
sources.claim: Profiler onRender exposes actualDuration for rendering the current subtree update and baseDuration estimating unoptimized render cost.

questions.prompt: Which memo claims are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A used context change can still cause rendering.
It replaces the requirement for pure component calculations.
It guarantees a component can never render again after mounting.
It can reduce renders driven by unchanged parent props.
A component can still render when its own state changes.

questions.explanation: A: Correct: context updates remain relevant. B: Incorrect: memoized components must still be pure. C: Incorrect: it does not freeze components. D: Correct: this is its optimization purpose. E: Correct: local updates still apply.

sources.title: memo
sources.claim: memo optimizes unchanged props, not local state or context updates, and does not remove purity requirements.

questions.prompt: Which claims about useMemo are true? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A missing dependency guarantees the result follows that value changes.
Its calculation should be pure.
A dependency newly created on every render can defeat caching.
It must be used as the only storage for required persistent application state.
It can reuse a result when dependencies are unchanged.

questions.explanation: A: Incorrect: omission can retain stale output. B: Correct: repeated calculations must be safe. C: Correct: changed reference identity invalidates comparison. D: Incorrect: memoization is an optimization rather than correctness storage. E: Correct: equal dependencies allow cached output.

questions.prompt: Which props can break default memo equality across otherwise similar parent renders? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The same already existing object reference passed again.
A freshly created callback function with equivalent behavior.
The same primitive boolean value passed again.
A newly allocated object containing the same fields.
The same primitive string value passed again.

questions.explanation: A: Incorrect: identical references compare equal. B: Correct: function references also differ. C: Incorrect: identical primitive booleans compare equal. D: Correct: new references differ. E: Incorrect: the same string compares equal.

sources.title: memo
sources.claim: Default memo comparison uses Object.is for individual props rather than deep comparison of object or function contents.

questions.prompt: Which claims support measured React performance decisions? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Profiler baseDuration estimates render cost without optimization.
Profiler actualDuration reports SQL transaction wait time.
Compare measured render costs before and after an optimization.
Browser paint time is identical to every Profiler render duration.
Profiler measures work rendering a React subtree.

questions.explanation: A: Correct: baseDuration estimates the subtree full render cost. B: Incorrect: it measures React rendering, not SQL. C: Correct: measurements show whether changes reduce work. D: Incorrect: browser painting is a different pipeline stage. E: Correct: Profiler wraps component trees.

sources.title: Profiler
sources.claim: Profiler reports render timing through actualDuration and baseDuration for evaluating performance changes.
